text:
maya: Taking over primary for the 9a-5p shift. Quick handoff: ongoing high-429 spike for hosted text-gen endpoints, customer-facing errors for some tenant buckets. I'm nearby for the next hour then will hand to sam.
incident-bot: Paging: @eng-oncall primary (maya) - High error rate detected on /v1/generate (429s). Alert id: A-4592. Severity: P2.
sam: thanks maya, I'm on standby. rough client impact?
maya: top-line: about 8% of requests in US-west are failing with 429. Not all customers — mostly medium throughput tenants hitting burst throttles. No data exfiltration.
jordan: do we have a routing/quotas change recently? I didn't see config rollouts.
maya: no config rollouts in last 6 hours. infra autoscaler kicked weirdly at 08:42, saw many short-lived pods.
lee: linking runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/429-throttle-handling (please use that for mitigation steps)
maya: quick checklist I'm running: 1) check quota logs 2) check router fallback counts 3) open temporary burst window for affected tenant(s) if safe 4) notify support/CS.
support-bot: New support ticket created for tenant "Acme-Apps" about API 429s. Ticket ID: S-8873. Assigned: rachel.
rachel: got it, I'll message the account rep and get a list of impacted endpoints/customers.
sam: if it's burst window quota, we should route heavy tails to dedicated pools (runtime) rather than shared. who owns routing policy right now? runtime or infra?
maya: routing policy config is owned by runtime, but infra enforces node/slot quotas. So cross-team touch: runtime to pin route, infra to open temporary capacity, security only if we see auth anomalies.
jordan: ok. I can look at runtime routing metrics to see if requests were misrouted to shared pools. Give me 5m.
(5 minutes pass)
jordan: from routing logs: ~73% of the failing requests were routed to shared-pool-eu-west rather than the tenant's reserved pool because cache key mismatch. There was a KV cache flush at 08:41. See logs:```
[08:41:12] cache.flushed keys=7321
[08:41:13] routing.decide tenant=acme auth=true preferred_pool=acme-reserved but selected=shared-pool-eu-west
[08:41:14] token.bucket check failed - burst exceeded
```
maya: that aligns. So two parallel mitigations: 1) runtime: fix routing cache key fallback to prefer reserved pool on miss (hotfix rule), 2) infra: temporarily increase burst tokens for shared-pool to reduce 429s while we deploy.
lee: infra can open a temporary capacity increase for shared-pool for 30 minutes. I'll start the change now, will post progress here.
security-oncall: quick note from security: unless there's anomalous auth patterns, no need to escalate to sec. If we see repeated auth failures or tokens reused multiple times, flag to us.
sam: timeline and owners: runtime (jordan) — implement hotfix rule + run a small canary. infra (lee) — temporary capacity + monitor. support (rachel) — client comms. i'll be secondary to coordinate fallbacks and rollback plan.
maya: I can implement a short-term routing override (pin to reserved pool) for Acme-Apps via console for the next 15m. Doing it now, will verify metrics after 2 minutes.
(2 minutes pass)
maya: override applied -> metrics: 429s for Acme down from 18% to 2% in first 90s. CPU on reserved pool increased ~12%. No errors seen.
jordan: pushing a small routing rule change to prefer reserved pool on cache-miss. will deploy to canary 1 then 3, then full if green.```
git log -1 --pretty=oneline
abc1234 runtime: prefer-reserved-on-cache-miss
```
lee: infra capacity change applied. shared-pool burst tokens +30% for 30m, monitor dashboards.
rachel: passed initial note to Acme support rep. holding on email until we confirm it's resolved for all endpoints.
sam: good. two followups: 1) we need a better alarm to distinguish cache-flush-induced routing failures vs genuine quota exhaustion; 2) handoff notes for next primary.
maya: agree. I'm writing a handoff blurb to paste into #oncall-log. Also creating a short post-incident task to add a routing-mismatch alert and add an entry to the runbook about KV cache flushes.
incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Incident A-4592 status: mitigated.
jordan: can we also add a temporary test so that KV cache flush doesn't immediately cause fallback to shared? Maybe a small grace window where we prefer last-known pool.
lee: infra will add smoothing to the token-bucket logic to prevent abrupt 0 windows after a cache flush. ETA: 2 days for code + 4hr config tune.
security-oncall: nothing suspicious so far, but leave me a note if auth error spikes.
maya: handing primary to sam at 10:15. Sam, my checklist: state of incident, who I paged, overrides applied, where to roll back (console -> routing overrides -> remove), links to dashboards + runbook.
sam: thanks — taking primary. I'll stay until 14:00 and confirm stability. If anything changes escalate to oncall-ops.
maya: posting handoff to oncall-log: "1732109876 - handoff: maya -> sam. Incident A-4592 mitigated. Applied routing override for Acme-Apps; infra temporary +30% burst; runtime hotfix canary in progress. Follow-ups: add routing-mismatch alert, KV-cache runbook entry, infra smoothing change"
rachel: I'll keep Acme updated and close ticket once we see 60m of stability across all endpoints.
sam: noted. tagging runbook sections: runbook steps followed: step 2 (identify impact), step 4 (routing override), step 5 (capacity increase), step 8 (client comms). Leaving this thread open for any residual checks.
incident-bot: Reminder: on-call rotation check-in due at handoff.
maya: thanks everyone. If anything pops up ping me direct, otherwise i'll be offline after 10:30.
lee: monitoring graphs look ok. I'll revert infra change after 30m unless we ask to extend.
jordan: will follow up with a PR to add the routing grace logic.
sam: closing loop — I'll update thread in 30m with final state.
(30 minutes later)
sam: final update: metrics stable, 429s returned to baseline. infra change reverted. closing incident.
incident-bot: Incident A-4592 closed. Duration: 0:47:32.
maya: thanks all for quick coordination :thumbsup:
